claims.statement: SystemOneMiddleware plays System 1's top move only when threshold < 1.0 and the gate signal (margin p1-p2 by default, or Choice confidence) is at least the threshold; otherwise it writes a top-k (or top_p prefix capped at k) shortlist as soft candidates, so threshold 0 always plays and threshold 1 never plays.

After a tournament, tournament_threshold replaces threshold when set (otherwise threshold applies), because a final over fewer moves inflates the margin and SemIf confidence depends on option count; the applied value is recorded as threshold_used.

The System 1 decision is frozen per turn in the private systemone_turn channel and replayed on every later before_model of the same turn instead of re-ranking, writing only current allowed ∩ frozen so later narrowing is never undone and skipped decisions replay as nothing.

In both played and shortlist outcomes SystemOneMiddleware writes System 1's top move as fallback_move (only if still allowed). The UCI adapter uses it as bestmove after a cancellation or execution failure only when the last turn belongs to that search and the move is in the root pool; otherwise it picks a seeded random pool move, or the null move 0000 if the pool is empty.

When ranking raises RankingFailed, a middleware with has_model=True records a skipped decision with the error and completed calls and lets the LLM choose unaided, while has_model=False re-raises so the run fails and the turn stays pending.
The tournament seed is turn_seed(agent_seed, turn_id), a SHA-256 of the agent seed and turn id (not hash()), so the shuffle is repeatable within a turn but differs across turns and games.

GatewayRanker ranks with no request when there is one option, with a single systemone.rank request when options fit the model cap (16 for semif-*, 255 for typesafe/jev-*, 16 for unknown models), and with a tournament traced as systemone.heats then systemone.final otherwise.

GatewayRanker retries only transient gateway errors (rate limit, connection, timeout, internal server error) up to max_attempts=3 with backoff min(4.0, 0.5*2**n) seconds, fails immediately on other errors, and raises RankingFailed carrying the calls completed before the failure.

Every Choice answer is validated against its own options: unknown labels, non-finite or out-of-range probabilities, an all-zero sum or a sum missing 1 beyond tolerance (widened for two-decimal rounding), and bad confidence raise MalformedChoice, which the ranker turns into RankingFailed while keeping the request's Call. Valid answers are only scaled down (divided by max(total, 1)), so a rounded-away shortfall is never inflated, and ties are broken by option order.

The rank request carries a facts-only state (side, FEN, board, material, check, recent SAN) and Choice criteria built from python-chess move facts including static exchange evaluation; the rich style is the default and descriptions are deterministic.

Optional eval Score and needs_calculation/tactics_present Noul questions are added only to the final (or single) request when with_eval/with_nouls are enabled and are recorded as telemetry without affecting the gate.

The tournament shuffles options with random.Random(seed), splits them into ceil(n/cap) balanced heats, advances floor(cap/h) per heat with spare places to the first heats (one each when heats exceed cap, recursing), records single-move heats as byes never sent, packs heats into requests of at most 32 questions, and ends with one final over the finalists.
After a tournament the distribution, shortlist and telemetry top list cover finalists only (flagged finalist_conditional), and each move's stages record per-round results rather than a global rank.
Each gateway request records a Call of kind systemone with provider typesafe; SemIf returns no usage so its calls have cost_usd None, while Jev calls are priced.

The server and CLI build SystemOneMiddleware for policy systemone with threshold 0, tournament_threshold 0 and has_model False, and pass the gate/threshold/tournament_threshold/k/top_p knobs for hybrid (default). For policy llm the server installs NoSystemOne while the CLI omits the middleware. The server builds the GatewayRanker itself with style, with_eval, with_nouls and a TypeSafeClassifier built from TYPESAFE_API_KEY/TYPESAFE_BASE_URL (required, else ValueError), while the CLI passes style/with_eval/with_nouls to the middleware, which builds its own default GatewayRanker.

SystemOneMiddleware telemetry is written to Ply.meta["SystemOneMiddleware"] as SystemOneMeta (status, model, top, shortlist, followed, gate, signal, confidence, margin, threshold_used, finalist_conditional, played_move_result, tournament, error, plus NotRequired latency_ms, eval_score, needs_calculation, tactics_present), and its TypedDicts are mirrored by hand in packages/chess-ui/src/types.ts, where latency_ms, the aux fields and top are optional.

SystemOneMeta.latency_ms is the ranker's wall time for the whole ranking: 0.0 for a local one-option distribution, and for a skipped decision the time the ranking ran before failing (RankingFailed.elapsed_ms). Telemetry is read from the frozen decision, so replays report the first ranking's values.

eval_score, needs_calculation and tactics_present come from an optional Score and two Noul questions that are added only to the aux-bearing (single or final) request when with_eval or with_nouls is enabled. Otherwise, or on skip, they are None, and the gate never uses them.

NoSystemOne has SystemOneMiddleware's name and SystemOneState schema but does nothing in before_model, so the server's fixed-topology graph (policy llm and the credential-free shape() graph) keeps the same nodes and state keys as a graph running System 1.

On the server, every System 1 TypeSafeClassifier uses one per-process httpx2 sync/async client pair from POOL (15 s timeout), created lazily under a lock; the FastAPI app lifespan closes it with POOL.aclose() on shutdown, after which get() creates a fresh pair. The pool lives in its own module because langgraph loads graph.py under a generated module name.

SystemOneMiddleware reports the frozen decision's ranking time through turn_latency_ms, so the ranking is counted once per turn across retries: a System 1 move's ply and turn latency equal the ranking time, and a hybrid turn adds it to model time.

With no injected client, GatewayRanker builds TypeSafeClassifier(model, timeout=15 s) lazily on first use so graph construction needs no credentials, and its async path builds the request (including move descriptions) in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread.
